name: Permitting and enforcement for seismic retrofits in Los Angeles
headline: Permitting and enforcement for seismic retrofits in Los Angeles
articleBody: In Los Angeles, seismic retrofit ordinances are implemented through standard building department permitting, plan review, inspection, and enforcement mechanisms. For the City of Los Angeles soft‑story program, the Department of Building and Safety identifies buildings that meet the ordinance criteria and issues an Order to Comply to owners, as documented in program descriptions shared by engineering and ordinance‑tracking resources. That Order formally initiates the retrofit process and sets specific deadlines. Owners must then hire licensed design professionals to prepare retrofit plans in accordance with the California Building Code and city‑adopted technical guidelines. These plans are submitted for plan check, where building officials review structural calculations, detailing, and compliance with ordinance provisions. After plan approval, the owner obtains a building permit for rehabilitation, and construction can begin. City inspectors visit the site at key stages—such as installation of anchors, frames, and shear walls—to verify compliance with approved plans. Enforcement occurs if owners fail to meet submittal, permit, or construction deadlines. The city’s published timeline outlines that missing milestones can lead to code enforcement actions. While specific penalty structures are governed by municipal code, structural engineering firms working in Los Angeles note that potential consequences include fines, notices of violation, and, in extreme cases, orders limiting occupancy or utilities for unsafe buildings. In unincorporated Los Angeles County, Public Works and Building and Safety departments similarly administer Chapter 95 tilt‑up requirements and the emerging high‑rise nonductile concrete ordinance through permitting and inspections. This means that for both city and County programs, seismic retrofits are integrated into standard construction regulatory workflows rather than handled as purely separate processes.
